title: Calling `Texture2D.get_image()` followed by `Image.blend_rect()` in `@tool` script causes imported Texture's data to be adjusted until reimport
body: ### Tested versions ~~Occured in 4.7.stable.~~ Reproducible in 4.7.stable ### System information Godot v4.7.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 4 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.16.1062) - AMD Ryzen 7 9700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.16 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description ~~I was working on using a `Image.get_region()` on the top half of an image. Surprisingly, the image, after being saved, showed it was a completely smeared image. The first pixel in each column was stretched until the bottom of the region image, creating vertical columns of pixels.~~ ~~_The input image, which uses transparency throughout._~~ ~~I switched to testing `Image.get_region()` on the entire image, which kept returning the same issue. The top half was completely smeared.~~ ~~_The output, with the top half being vertically stretched_~~ ~~When I tested this with other images, I couldn't reproduce it at all. They just seemed to work normally and as expected. After checking the **Import Settings** of the image, I noticed the `Roughness/Mode` was set to `7` and the `SRC Normal` image was set different image in the folder (which was not a roughness image at all).~~ ~~After switching the mode back from `7` to `Detect`, the issue disappeared. Since the enum for `Roughness/Mode` does not allow me to switch back to `7`, I cannot reproduce it anymore. But the fact that it showed an int, rather than an enum value probably means something went wrong there.~~ ~~I have never adjusted the import settings for this image manually. But the Texture2D default has `Fix Alpha Border = false` and `Detect 3D/Compress To = disabled` set.~~ When using an `@export` texture in a `@tool` script, and retrieving the image from the texture with `get_image()`, a `blend_rect()` adjustment of the image will also be applied to the imported image. This is in contradiction with the documentation that states `get_image()` returns a copy of the data. You can see this when looking at the preview in the FileSystem: ### Steps to reproduce ~~1. Import the following images into Godot~~ ~~_(I believe the images were imported at the same time when I first created them)_~~ ~~2. Set the Roughness/Mode in the import settings for `7` and add the `border_only` image as the `Src Normal`. In my case Godot somehow did this itself.~~ ~~3. Run the following function:~~ ``` var testimage = image.get_region(Rect2i(Vector2(0,0), image.get_size())) testimage.save_png("res://testimage_region.png") ``` ~~4. The output image will not return the original image, but will have certain pixels stretched.~~ ~~I'm afraid that's all the information I have. It is likely not reproducible consistently, since it seems to be a `get_region()` issue in conjunction with an `Import` issue. But perhaps other users have more information, or further investigation will still lead to the cause being found.~~ EDIT: 1. Import the image (presumably any image will do though) 2. Create a tool script with ``` @tool @export var cluster_texture : Texture @export_tool_button("Break Image Data") var testbutton= create_blend_image func create_blend_image(): var image = cluster_texture.get_image() image.blend_rect(image, Rect2i(0,0, image.get_width(), image.get_height() / 2), Vector2(0,1)) image.save_png("res://testimage_region.png") ``` 3. Add the texture as the exported variable. 4. Press the tool button to blend the image. 5. The export image will look messed up (thats expected, but a nice indication) 6. Remove the `blend_rect` line 7. Reload the tool scene, to be sure the tool script is fully up-to-date 8. Run the script again 9. The saved image will keep the artifacts, because the data it gains from `texture.get_image()` is messed up. It will keep returning the blended image, until the texture is reimported. 10. Hover the preview in the FileSystem of the image, it will show the artefacts as well.### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) I cannot create a minimal reproduction project that shows the issue anymore
